content.rendered:
And so we’ve reached the end of the Cover Me series.

It’s incomplete, as it was always destined to be. Trying to catalog and chronicle every song Bruce Springsteen has ever covered is the very definition of chasing a moving target.

Even so, I’m sure some of you will notice the absence of a few classics. I’m at peace with it, though. John Fogerty has so many entries in this series that I can forgive myself for never getting around to “Proud Mary.” (I did write an entry for “Travelin’ Band” specifically for this book, though. That one I couldn’t leave out.)

There is, however, one particular cover that will probably render you aghast if and when you realize its omission.

About that I will only say this: I left it out on purpose, because from my very first day as a blogger, I knew it would be the last essay I would ever write about  Bruce Springsteen. It’ll see publication as the last entry in Volume 50 of the Bookshelf Collection sometime in late 2027 or early 2028.

For now, thanks for reading my Cover Me posts over the years, even though I know many of you were hoping each day for a Roll of the Dice entry instead.

Cover Me was the series I always enjoyed writing the most.  I hope you enjoy reading final collection.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Spare Parts: Cheap Motel
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Co-written but never performed by Bruce, Joe Grushecky's "Cheap Motel" sure *sounds* like a Bruce song. Take a listen inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Walking Through Midnight
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One of the more under-the-radar Southside Johnny/Bruce Springsteen collaborations, "Walking Through Midnight" closed Southside's first solo album in 1988.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: Twenty More Miles
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Tucked into the end of Steel Mill's set-closing cover of Richie Havens' "Run, Shaker Life" is this very under-the-radar Springsteen original.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hoochie Coochie Man
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Almost 50 years ago, The Bruce Springsteen Band put their own stamp on Muddy Waters' biggest hit. Listen to their absolutely epic "Hoochie Coochie Man" inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cover Me, Cleveland School of Rock: Trapped
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: If you ever wonder whether Bruce's music will stay relevant to new generations, watch this clip of the Cleveland School of Rock performing "Trapped" and put your mind at ease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Walking the Dog
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The early E Street Band had a lot in common with the late Bruce Springsteen Band, and nowhere was that more apparent than in their cover of Rufus Thomas' "Walking the Dog."
